review_precision_corrections: 112: hold primarily for arbitrary constraints not necessarily defining lower-dimensional manifolds; active-set clause is solver-dependent, not an asserted exhaustive/NP-hard theorem.

records.rationale: Correct branch-by-branch set construction for a piecewise domain, considering both the formula and the condition before taking the union.

evidence.finding: A branch contributes the intersection of its formula domain with its condition set; taking the union of those intersections gives the inputs where some prescribed branch applies.
Overlapping branches must also agree or have a defined priority to specify a single-valued function, but that is separate from identifying allowable inputs.

records.rationale: The finite-dimensional module-theoretic connections are useful, but the required finite-dimensional/torsion hypotheses are not stated. A general operator on an arbitrary vector space need not have a minimal or characteristic polynomial, and a Jordan form also needs a splitting field.

evidence.title: Romyar Sharifi, UCLA Abstract Algebra, section 8.10
evidence.finding: The module decomposition and canonical forms use a finite-dimensional vector space; Jordan form over F additionally requires that the characteristic polynomial split over F.
On V=F[x], let T be multiplication by x. For any nonzero polynomial p, p(T)(1)=p(x)!=0, so T has no annihilating minimal polynomial. Its F[x]-module is free rather than finite torsion.
For finite-dimensional V, eigenspace means the submodule annihilated by x-lambda; higher-power primary torsion gives the generalized eigenspace.

records.rationale: Correct dimensions and entrywise algorithm for matrix multiplication, with the right associativity and general noncommutativity distinction.

evidence.finding: For conformable finite matrices, (AB)_ij=sum_k A_ik B_kj. Distributivity and associativity prove product associativity; counterexamples show multiplication need not commute.

records.rationale: The two rational examples share exactly the stated vertical and horizontal asymptotes and differ in sign and pole order, proving asymptotes do not determine a graph.

records.rationale: The row-reduction method and determinant bookkeeping are correct, but a fastest-by-hand claim cannot be made from size alone. The answer overstates that it is much faster than expansion without inspecting zeros or special structure.

evidence.finding: Adding a multiple of one row to another preserves determinant; a row swap negates it, nonzero scaling changes it by that scalar, and a triangular matrix determinant is its diagonal product.

evidence.title: Georgia Tech, Interactive Linear Algebra: Determinants and Cofactors
evidence.finding: Cofactor expansion can exploit rows or columns with many zeros; method choice depends on matrix structure.
For a matrix with an all-zero row, expansion along that row immediately gives determinant zero. A row with one nonzero entry can also make cofactor expansion preferable to a general reduction.

records.rationale: Correct geometric image and determinant-area interpretation, with negative determinant reversing orientation.

evidence.finding: The images of the two unit coordinate vectors are the columns of the matrix; the image square is their possibly degenerate parallelogram with area equal to absolute determinant.

records.rationale: Correct proof-by-contradiction method for nonexistence, assuming all substitutions and deductions preserve the specified domain.

evidence.finding: A contradiction from the hypothesis that a solution exists proves nonexistence. Definitions fix meanings; axioms give assumed properties in the specified structure.

records.rationale: Accurate description of solving a triangular system from its final equation upward.

evidence.finding: If the complete equation a_k x=b_k is a linear combination of remaining equations with the same coefficients on both sides, every solution of the remaining equations satisfies it. Deleting it preserves the solution set.
This describes ordinary nonsingular back substitution; zero pivots require separate consistency/free-variable handling.

records.rationale: Sound introductory distinction between concrete elementary algebra and reasoning from abstract structural axioms.

evidence.finding: A symbolic identity or implication derived from stated algebraic axioms proves all covered instances; a finite list of numerical tests does not establish an unrestricted universal statement.
The distinction is pedagogical rather than a claim that elementary algebra lacks axioms or that abstract algebra never concerns numbers.

evidence.finding: Adding a multiple of one row to another preserves determinant; a row swap negates it, nonzero scaling changes it by that scalar, and a triangular matrix determinant is its diagonal product.
Any permutation decomposes into transpositions. Each swap contributes a factor -1 from determinant alternation, so the final value is +1 or -1.

records.rationale: Correct practical distinction between statements assumed within a theory and definitions specifying terminology, illustrated with groups and normal subgroups.

evidence.finding: A contradiction from the hypothesis that a solution exists proves nonexistence. Definitions fix meanings; axioms give assumed properties in the specified structure.
Group axioms are also part of the definition of a group; they are assumptions for any object being treated as one.

evidence.title: Boyd and Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization
evidence.finding: Inequality-constrained convex problems can be solved by continuous optimization techniques such as interior-point methods; not all inequalities force combinatorial active-set enumeration.

The equality xy=0 is singular at the origin, while x>=0 defines a full-dimensional half-space. These refute a universal lower-dimensional-manifold description. Interior-point algorithms illustrate a different inequality-handling approach, but do not show that active-set identification has no combinatorial aspect.

records.rationale: The warning that a few examples do not prove an unrestricted identity is correct, but the blanket statement that examples never cover all possibilities excludes legitimate exhaustive proof on a finite domain.

evidence.finding: If a finite collection of cases covers the domain and the proposition is proved in every case, any putative counterexample belongs to a proved case and is impossible.
To prove a property for the set {0,1}, checking both elements exhausts every possibility. That differs from a few evaluations of the unrestricted difference-of-squares identity.

evidence.title: Tojaga et al., Hybrid of monolithic and staggered solution techniques
evidence.finding: This coupled fracture model has reduced monolithic robustness from non-positive-definite tangent stiffness; alternating solution avoids that difficulty but has suboptimal convergence, motivating a hybrid. The comparison is problem-dependent.
The frequency and professional-quality language is qualitative advice; it is not treated as an empirical probability or a universal impossibility result.

records.rationale: The coupling overview is useful, but the recommended element-based elimination is under-specified for general reactive species transport. Element balances constrain composition but do not determine the remaining species or reaction progress without kinetic, equilibrium or independent-progress equations.

evidence.title: Cantera, Chemical Reactions
evidence.finding: Chemical kinetics computes species reaction rates from rate constants and the mixture state, including composition and temperature. Conserved elemental totals do not alone specify species composition or reaction progress.
Two moles H2 plus one mole O2 and two moles H2O both contain four H atoms and two O atoms, yet represent different species states. Conserved element totals alone cannot select between them.
A coordinate transformation using conserved elements plus independent progress variables can be valid; the hold targets the missing closure, not all elimination strategies.
